title: Neon Descent
premise: A glowing courier block descends through a futuristic grid while the player dodges falling jammer hazards for as long as possible.
interaction_model: Single-screen real-time arcade survival controlled by drag, tap, or pointer movement to reposition horizontally.
objective: Avoid all falling jammers, survive as long as possible, and maximize distance while advancing through rising zone numbers.
progression: Endless score attack structure where distance increases over time, zones rise at score thresholds, obstacle speed grows, and spawn intervals shorten until the player crashes.
theme: Neon cyber-grid courier escape under signal-jammer pressure.
mood: Tense, fast, reactive, futuristic, and arcade-like.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy quick mobile-friendly reflex games, endless survival challenges, and minimalist neon arcade presentation.
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is an endless survival dodging game because score increments over time and the only fail state is collision.
High confidence in pointer-based horizontal control because input sets a target X value and the player only moves left/right.
Moderate confidence that the fiction is a courier navigating jammers, because the UI text frames the avatar as a courier and enemies as jammers.
Moderate confidence that it fits runner-like categories despite lacking forward movement controls, because the scrolling grid and distance-based survival evoke an endless runner structure.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished mobile-friendly browser arcade game called "Neon Descent" presented entirely on a full-screen canvas with a layered neon HUD. The fantasy is that the player is guiding a glowing courier through a hostile digital grid while jammer blocks rain down from above. Place the player avatar near the bottom of the screen as a cyan glowing square with a bright center, and restrict movement to left and right only. Controls should be simple and touch-first: dragging, tapping, or pointer movement sets a horizontal target, and the courier smoothly slides toward that point with a capped speed for a responsive but readable feel. Build the core gameplay as an endless survival run. The score should represent DISTANCE and increase continuously over time. Show a ZONE indicator that rises at score thresholds to communicate difficulty growth. Spawn enemy jammer blocks from random horizontal positions above the screen; make them red or magenta glowing squares with slight rotation as they fall. As the run continues, increase difficulty by making jammers fall faster and by shortening the spawn interval, creating a mounting dodge challenge. Any collision between the courier and a jammer should immediately end the run. Use presentation to sell the experience: draw a dark sci-fi background with moving holographic grid lines, subtle scanline energy, bloom-like glow, and a premium neon interface. Include a HUD at the top for DISTANCE and ZONE, and a bottom-centered status chip that can temporarily warn the player when an incoming jammer reaches the lower danger zone, using alert text like "JAMMER LOCK" and a short danger message. Add arcade juice such as screen shake on death, glowing particle explosions for both the courier and the obstacle on impact, and crisp transitions between states. Include light but effective audio design: looping gameplay music during runs, a restart/start cue when a new run begins, warning audio when danger spikes, a progression cue when the player reaches a new zone beat, and a distinct game-over sound on collision. After failure, hide the active HUD and show a centered game-over overlay with the title, a concise instruction telling the player to guide the courier left and right to dodge falling jammers, the final DISTANCE, and a replay button labeled with a stylish sci-fi phrase. The overall tone should be tense, sleek, futuristic, and highly replayable, like a minimalist endless runner reimagined as a horizontal dodge survival game.
